cues.en: Electricity faces a fundamental problem that comes with pretty much any product that's provided on demand.
cues.zh: 电力面临一个根本性问题，几乎所有按需提供的产品都会遇到。

cues.en: Our ability to generate large amounts of it doesn't match up that closely with when we need it. Wind and solar are becoming more cost effective, but they'll always be unreliable and intermittent sources of energy.
cues.zh: 我们的发电能力与用电需求时间并不完全匹配。风能和太阳能正变得越来越经济，但它们始终是不可靠且间歇性的能源。

cues.en: Retailers use warehouses to store goods between manufacture and sale. Water utilities use tanks and reservoirs. But the storage of electricity for later use, especially on a large scale, is more a challenging.
cues.zh: 零售商利用仓库在制造和销售之间储存商品。自来水公司使用水箱和水库。但将电力储存起来以备后用，尤其是大规模储存，则更具挑战性。

cues.en: That's why power grids are mostly real time systems with generation ramped up or down to meet fluctuating demands instantaneously.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么电网大多是实时系统，发电量会根据波动的需求即时增减。

cues.en: That's not to say though that we don't store energy at grid scale and there's one type of storage that makes up the vast majority of our current capacity. Hey, I'm Grady, and this is Practical Engineering. On today's episode, we're talking about pump storage hydroelectricity.
cues.zh: 不过，这并不意味着我们没有在电网规模上储存能量，而且有一种储能方式构成了我们当前产能的绝大部分。嘿，我是Grady，这里是Practical Engineering。在今天的节目中，我们要讨论的是抽水蓄能水电。

cues.en: Although it's a very convenient form of energy to produce, transmit and use, electricity has some disadvantages.
cues.zh: 尽管电力是一种非常方便的生产、传输和使用形式，但它也有缺点。

cues.en: We've talked a little bit about the variability in demand and generation capacity in previous videos of this series, but I'll summarize again here.
cues.zh: 在本系列之前的视频中，我们已经讨论过需求和发电能力的可变性，但我在这里再总结一下。

cues.en: The fundamental problem is that we use electricity like this with peaks in the morning and evening, but we generate electricity differently.
cues.zh: 根本问题在于，我们像这样用电，早晚出现高峰，但发电方式却不同。

cues.en: Fossil fuel and nuclear plants generally have a single capacity at which they run most efficiently with occasional need to go offline for maintenance.
cues.zh: 化石燃料和核电厂通常有一个最经济的运行容量，偶尔需要停机维护。

cues.en: Solar, of course, follows the amount of sunlight with some variability due to clouds, and wind follows weather patterns with potential for lots of variability.
cues.zh: 太阳能当然随日照量变化，还会因云层而有些波动；风能则随天气模式变化，波动可能很大。

cues.en: You may have heard of the duck curve, which is the name given to our electricity demand minus the contribution from solar.
cues.zh: 你可能听说过鸭子曲线，它指的是用电需求减去太阳能贡献后的曲线。

cues.en: You end up with this funky curve representing the need for other sources of electricity.
cues.zh: 最终得到一条形状奇特的曲线，代表对其他电力来源的需求。

cues.en: This creates a challenge because not only does solar power start to die away right when we need it most during peak demands in the evening, it also creates a much steeper demand curve requiring grid operators to spin up other types of generation more quickly.
cues.zh: 这带来了挑战：太阳能恰好在傍晚用电高峰、我们最需要它的时候开始衰减，同时还造成需求曲线陡增，电网运营商必须更快启动其他类型的发电。

cues.en: So, solar power is meeting some of our electricity needs, but it's not necessarily eliminating
cues.zh: 所以，太阳能满足了部分用电需求，但未必能消除

cues.en: the need for other sources of electricity.
cues.zh: 对其他电力来源的需求。

cues.en: And in some cases, it may actually be making the grid less efficient by contributing to instability and requiring the use of peaking plants that are generally heavier polluters.
cues.zh: 在某些情况下，它实际上可能降低电网效率，因为它会加剧不稳定性，并需要使用通常污染更重的调峰电厂。

cues.en: In fact, peaking plants are the go to solution for load following on the grid. These are smaller, more expensive sources of electricity that only run for a few hours per day to make up the difference between the base power load and the evening peaks.
cues.zh: 事实上，调峰电厂是电网负荷跟踪的常用方案。它们是规模更小、成本更高的电力来源，每天只运行几个小时，以填补基础负荷与傍晚高峰之间的差额。

cues.en: Another interesting solution to this problem is called demand management, which is influencing the demand for electricity to reduce or shift peaks and match generation capacity better.
cues.zh: 这个问题的另一个有趣解决方案叫需求管理，就是影响用电需求，来削减或转移高峰，更好地匹配发电能力。

cues.en: This can be as simple as marketing campaigns encouraging you to set your thermostat a few degrees higher to sophisticated
cues.zh: 这可以简单到营销活动鼓励你把恒温器调高几度，也可以复杂到

cues.en: systems that can tell your electric car when to start charging. But, the holy grail in grid scale power delivery is simply to let the demand and generation curves be what they'll be storing energy when generation exceeds demand and using that stored energy during demand peaks.
cues.zh: 能告诉你的电动车什么时候开始充电的系统。但在电网级电力输送中，终极目标就是让需求和发电曲线顺其自然，在发电超过需求时储存能量，在需求高峰时使用储存的能量。

cues.en: There are a wide variety of fascinating ideas for storing large amounts of energy from molten salt to pressurizing the air in old mines, but most of our current grid scale storage relies on gravitational potential.
cues.zh: 储存大量能量的有趣想法有很多，从熔盐到给废弃矿井里的空气加压，但我们目前大多数电网级储能都依赖重力势能。

cues.en: That is using excess energy to lift something up and then using that thing to generate electricity as it falls back down, essentially treating the earth's gravity like a spring. And the vast majority of our current grid scale storage does this using water in a scheme called pump storage hydroelectricity.
cues.zh: 就是用多余的能量把东西抬起来，然后让它落下来时发电，本质上把地球重力当成弹簧。目前绝大多数电网级储能都是用水来实现的，方案叫抽水蓄能。

cues.en: And I built a little mini scale version of this as a demonstration.
cues.zh: 我做了个迷你版来演示。

cues.en: In most cases, the way this works is to have two reservoirs nearby but separated by a large difference in elevation.
cues.zh: 大多数情况下，做法是在附近建两个水库，但海拔差很大。

cues.en: In this case, two buckets separated by a ladder. At night, when electricity prices are low, you can use that cheap power and pumps to fill the upper reservoir.
cues.zh: 这里就是两个桶，中间隔着一把梯子。晚上电价低的时候，你可以用廉价电力和水泵把上水库灌满。

cues.en: During the day when energy prices are high,
cues.zh: 白天电价高的时候，

cues.en: you use the water in the upper reservoir to spin turbines and generate hydropower.
cues.zh: 你就用上水库的水驱动涡轮机发电。

cues.en: It's essentially a giant water battery and storing energy in this way has a lot of benefits besides just shaving off the peaks of the demand curve.
cues.zh: 它本质上就是一个巨大的水电池，这种储能方式除了削峰之外还有很多好处。

cues.en: Hydropower is one of the most responsive ways to generate electricity,
cues.zh: 水力发电是响应最快的发电方式之一，

cues.en: so pumped storage allows grid operators to handle fluctuations in demand quickly.
cues.zh: 所以抽水蓄能让电网调度员快速应对需求波动。

cues.en: Pumped storage is also valuable in an emergency, providing quick access to power when other sources may be out of commission.
cues.zh: 抽水蓄能在紧急情况下也很有价值，当其他电源可能无法运行时，它能快速提供电力。

cues.en: Finally, these systems can provide a lot of benefit on small insular power grids like on islands where you don't have as much diversification
cues.zh: 最后，这类系统在小型孤立电网上能带来很大好处，比如在岛屿上，那里的发电组合没有那么多样的

cues.en: in the generation portfolio.
cues.zh: 发电来源。

cues.en: But, pump storage has several major challenges as well and I'll use this demo to illustrate the big ones.
cues.zh: 但抽水蓄能也有几个重大挑战，我用这个演示来说明主要的几个。

cues.en: First is energy density, which is the term used to describe how much energy can fit into unit volume.
cues.zh: 首先是能量密度，这个词用来描述单位体积能容纳多少能量。

cues.en: And, this is not a pump storage facility's finest feature.
cues.zh: 而这并不是抽水蓄能设施最擅长的方面。

cues.en: Just for some reference, here's the energy density of gasoline,
cues.zh: 供参考，这是汽油的能量密度、

cues.en: a lithium ion battery, and the water in a typical pump storage reservoir.
cues.zh: 锂离子电池的能量密度，以及典型抽水蓄能水库中水的能量密度。

cues.en: I say typical because the total energy storage is both a function of height and volume.
cues.zh: 我说典型，是因为总储能既取决于高度也取决于体积。

cues.en: The greater the head above the turbines, the more the generating capacity for a given volume of water.
cues.zh: 涡轮机上方的水头越大，给定水量下的发电能力就越强。

cues.en: I'm using a little aquarium pump to fill up my upper reservoir on top of this ladder.
cues.zh: 我正用一个小水族箱水泵，往梯子顶部的上蓄水池注水。

cues.en: It's pretty easy to see the difference in energy density between a battery and the stored water.
cues.zh: 很容易看出电池和蓄水之间的能量密度差异。

cues.en: The water in this bucket has about the same gravitational
cues.zh: 这个桶里的水所具有的重力

cues.en: potential energy as the battery in your car's key fob.
cues.zh: 势能，大概和你车钥匙里的电池相当。

cues.en: In fact, to reach the same density as a typical lithium ion battery, you'd have to have the water stored at a height of approximately
cues.zh: 事实上，要想达到普通锂离子电池的能量密度，你得把水储存在大约

cues.en: outside the earth's atmosphere,
cues.zh: 地球大气层外的高度，

cues.en: which wouldn't be very convenient for an electric vehicle.
cues.zh: 这对电动汽车来说可不太方便。

cues.en: In fact, this is one of the main disadvantages of pump storage facilities is that they require a very specific type of site where you can locate two pools near each other while also separating them by as much vertical distance as possible.
cues.zh: 事实上，抽水蓄能设施的主要缺点之一，就是对选址要求极高：既要让两个水池彼此靠近，又要尽可能拉开它们的垂直落差。

cues.en: And, even then, because of the low energy density,
cues.zh: 而且，即便如此，由于能量密度低，

cues.en: these are often massive reservoirs that are major civil engineering projects as compared to something like a battery that can be manufactured in a factory.
cues.zh: 这些设施通常都是巨大的水库，属于大型土木工程项目，而不像电池那样可以直接在工厂制造。

cues.en: The other major challenge with pump storage is getting the energy back out once you've stored it. Efficiency is the ratio of how much energy you put in versus how much you get out. You never get it all. That's the second law of thermodynamics.
cues.zh: 抽水蓄能的另一个主要挑战，在于存进去的能量如何再取出来。效率就是输出能量与输入能量的比值。你永远不可能百分之百收回，这就是热力学第二定律。

cues.en: But, you hope you get most of it. Otherwise, you built a very big, very expensive battery that doesn't work.
cues.zh: 但你总希望能收回大部分。否则，你只是造了一个又大又贵却毫无用处的电池。

cues.en: As I mentioned, my model reservoir is holding about a tenth of a watt hour, but that's not how much energy it took to get it there.
cues.zh: 正如我刚才提到的，我的模型水库蓄存了大约 0.1 瓦时的能量，但这并不是把水抽上去所消耗的能量。

cues.en: I kept an eye on the power supply while the bucket filled and it took almost seven tenths of a watt hour of electricity.
cues.zh: 水桶注水的过程中我留意了电源，总共消耗了近 0.7 瓦时的电量。

cues.en: That means my pump's efficiency was about 15%,
cues.zh: 这意味着我这台水泵的效率只有大约 15%，

cues.en: so the most energy I can even hope to recover is a lot less than I put in.
cues.zh: 所以理论上我能回收的最大能量，也远少于我投入的电量。

cues.en: Some pump storage facilities can use reversible pumps that act as turbines,
cues.zh: 有些抽水蓄能设施可以使用兼作水轮机的可逆式水泵，

cues.en: but in my case, I'm using a dedicated unit. I've got a power resistor as a dummy load and I'm measuring the voltage and current produced by the turbine to estimate the total recovery of energy. And the numbers don't look good. In fact, with a small amount of pressure, my little mini hydro turbine could barely spin at all. My best estimate is that I was able to generate two milliwatt hours from the full bucket. That's a whopping 0.3%
cues.zh: 但在我这里，我用的是独立机组。我接了一个功率电阻作为假负载，通过测量水轮机产生的电压和电流来估算总共回收的能量。数据看起来很不乐观。事实上在水压很小时，我的微型水轮机几乎根本转不动。据我最乐观的估计，这一满桶水大概能发出 2 毫瓦时的电。也就是惨淡的 0.3%

cues.en: efficiency.
cues.zh: 效率。

cues.en: And this is the other reason we're not hooking up tanks of water to our portable electronic devices.
cues.zh: 这也是我们为什么不会把水箱接到便携式电子设备上的另一个原因。

cues.en: At a small scale, this just isn't a feasible way to store power. Little pumps and turbines just aren't very efficient.
cues.zh: 在微观尺度下，这根本不是可行的储能方案。小型水泵和水轮机的效率实在太低了。

cues.en: But things look a lot better at large scale.
cues.zh: 但在宏观规模下，情况就好得多。

cues.en: Even considering all the potential losses of energy from evaporation
cues.zh: 就算把蒸发造成的潜在能量损失，

cues.en: or leakage of water to friction and turbulence within the machinery, many pump storage facilities achieve efficiencies of 70%
cues.zh: 以及漏水、机械内部的摩擦和湍流损耗都算进去，许多抽水蓄能设施的效率依然能达到 70%

cues.en: or higher.
cues.zh: 甚至更高。

cues.en: Of course, that means they are net energy consumers since, as we mentioned, you can't cover all the power used to pump the water to the top. But, if the cost of energy consumed is lower than the price they can get out of that energy minus inefficiencies during peak demand, they can still turn a profit.
cues.zh: 当然，这意味着它们是净能源消耗者，因为正如我们提到的，把水抽到高处所消耗的电力无法全部回收。但如果消耗的能源成本，低于它们在用电高峰期间从这些能源中获得的收益扣除效率损失后的部分，它们仍然可以盈利。

cues.en: In fact, you might be surprised how many pump storage facilities actually exist.
cues.zh: 事实上，实际存在的抽水蓄能设施数量之多可能会让你吃惊。

cues.en: In The US, the Energy Information Administration has a nice online map where you can go look around and see if there's one near you that you can go visit.
cues.zh: 在美国，能源信息管理局有一张很好用的在线地图，你可以去浏览一下，看看附近有没有可以参观的抽水蓄能设施。

cues.en: Of course, I only had time to go into the basics of pump storage, and there are a lot of interesting advancements on the horizon,
cues.zh: 当然，我只来得及介绍抽水蓄能的基础知识，而未来还有很多有趣的进展，

cues.en: like using abundantly available seawater instead of sometimes limited sources of freshwater.
cues.zh: 比如使用储量丰富的海水，而不是有时有限的淡水资源。

cues.en: Like demand management, pump storage is just one part of increasing the efficiency
cues.zh: 与需求管理一样，抽水蓄能只是提升效率

cues.en: and stability of power grid as we work to implement more renewable and sustainable sources of electricity.
cues.zh: 以及电网稳定性的一部分——我们正努力采用更多可再生和可持续的电力来源。
